moat_against: Contract value growth has collapsed and stayed down: from the 12-16% management calls normal to 1% in Q4 2025 and only 1.7% in Q2 2026 — two years of stall is erosion evidence, not just a cycle print
Wallet retention fell below 100% (98.2% in Q2 2026 vs 101.3% a year earlier): the existing client base is now shrinking its spend, and client enterprises fell 4.5% YoY to 12,775

Generative AI is a live substitution threat: buyers increasingly start vendor research by asking an LLM, and boutiques, peer-review platforms (G2 — which bought the divested Digital Markets properties) and free vendor content attack the same budget
People asset: the product is analyst judgment — analysts can leave, and the research must be re-earned every subscription cycle; no owned distribution or hard switching lock-in

Growth engine has quietly switched to financial engineering: TTM buybacks of $2.64B ran at ~2x free cash flow, funded with debt (net debt $0.53B at end-2024 to $1.26B at end-2025), which cannot persist at this pace
moat_for: Standard-setting brand: the Magic Quadrant is the enterprise tech-buying shortlist format — vendors must engage Gartner to be placed, buyers budget-hold around its advice; a two-sided flywheel (buyer attention attracts vendors, vendor engagement funds the research)

Subscription economics: Insights is the large majority of revenue on mostly multiyear contracts, 77% contribution margin in Q2 2026, and clients prepay — deferred revenue of $2.81B at end-2025 funds the business interest-free

Retention that holds even in a stall: wallet retention 98.2% and client retention 85.2% (rising sequentially) in Q2 2026, with contract value per enterprise up ~10% YoY to $414,000 — pricing power inside the installed base

Returns on capital far above the cost of capital through the cycle: roic_proxy in fundamentals.json 36% (2021), 43% (2022), 52% (2023), 55% (2024), 49% (2025), with gross margin stable at 68-70% over the same five years — the franchise needs almost no tangible capital (PP&E $214M on $6.5B revenue)
moat_justification: Strong moat, 7/10: the Magic Quadrant standard and the buyer/vendor two-sided flywheel, multiyear prepaid subscriptions at a 77% Insights contribution margin, 98%+ wallet retention even in the current stall, and measured returns on capital far above the cost of capital through the cycle (roic_proxy 36-55% over 2021-25 in fundamentals.json; management cited 31% rolling four-quarter ROIC on the Q2 2026 call) with gross margin pinned at 68-70% for five years. Not 8+: contract value growth has been stuck at 1-2% for two years, wallet retention has slipped below 100%, and generative AI is a credible substitution path for exactly the synthesis work Gartner sells — the moat is real but its growth engine is impaired.
name: Gartner, Inc.
one_liner: Elite subscription research franchise, moat 7/10 — but contract value growth has stalled at ~2% for two years and per-share growth now leans on debt-funded buybacks; at $205.35 the weighted IRR is 13.12% (Tier C) and it clears 15% only at or below $172.46.
